artists.biography: Robbie Robertson, OC (born Jaime Robert Klegerman; July 5, 1943) is a Canadian singer-songwriter and guitarist. He is best known for his work as lead guitarist and primary songwriter within The Band. He was ranked 59th in Rolling Stone magazine’s list of the 100 Greatest Guitarists of All Time.The Band has been inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and the Canadian Music Hall of Fame. As a songwriter, Robertson is credited for such songs as "The Weight", "The Night They Drove Old Dixie Down", "Up On Cripple Creek", "Broken Arrow" and "Somewhere Down the Crazy River", and has been inducted into the Canadian Songwriters Hall of Fame.

perplexity.description:
Robbie Robertson's 1987 self-titled debut marked a significant departure from his work with The Band, trading the group's intimate, roots-oriented approach for a more expansive, contemporary sound. Released on Geffen Records, the album showcased Robertson's evolution as a solo artist while maintaining the songwriting quality that defined his earlier career. Working with producer Daniel Lanois, Robertson embraced modern production techniques and exotic instrumentation, moving away from the back-porch aesthetic that characterized The Band's music.

The album benefited from high-profile collaborations that reflected Lanois's connections in the contemporary rock world. U2 members appeared on two tracks—"Sweet Fire of Love" and "Testimony"—while Peter Gabriel contributed to the atmospheric "Fallen Angel," a tribute to deceased Band member Richard Manuel. These collaborations yielded mixed results; while Gabriel's presence enhanced the otherworldly quality of "Fallen Angel," Robertson's attempts to match U2's bombast on "Testimony" and "Sweet Fire of Love" occasionally felt uneven. Standout tracks like "American Roulette," featuring an extended guitar solo and instrumental outro, demonstrated Robertson's continued mastery of the instrument.

Commercially and critically, the album achieved solid success. It peaked at number 38 on both the Billboard 200 and UK Album Charts, earning gold certifications in the United States, United Kingdom, and Canada, with multiple platinum certifications in Canada. The album won the Juno Award for Album of the Year, with Robertson and Lanois also receiving the Producer of the Year award. Singles like "Showdown at Big Sky" reached number 2 on the Billboard Mainstream Rock Tracks chart, establishing Robertson as a viable solo artist beyond his Band legacy.
